correctness.rationale: A tree with E edges has shortest full-cover u-to-v walk 2E-d(u,v). From the established Munn Green-class interpretation, D/R/L minimal lengths optimize the diameter and endpoint eccentricities. Every Munn vertex is one of n+1 prefix group values, whose equality is decidable in deterministic logspace via Lipton–Zalcstein or the explicit Sanov modular calculation. Counting novel prefix values uses only log-sized indices. For a fixed pair of prefixes, the unique path consists exactly of the undirected walk-edge types occurring an odd number of times; count first occurrences and parity using equality of endpoints, storing only O(log n) bits. Maximizing distances over prefix index pairs is likewise logspace; comparing the resulting O(log n)-bit length expressions decides all three languages. Actual checker verified 21,845 words, 87,380 class comparisons and 26,093 independent parity-distance/modular pairs. Finite evidence is supporting, not the proof.

It does not give a deterministic logspace algorithm. The 1977 theorem of Lipton and Zalcstein supplies free-group equality in logspace but not the new edge-parity computation of all Munn distances, their extrema, and Green-representative membership. The precise claim is the deterministic logspace classification for three Green languages. Related published word-problem and conjugacy-language articles do not give the claimed Green representative predicate. Direct research-index and literature queries found no dominating equivalence. The result is a concise combination of prior theorems and a new logspace computation, so originality has qualified residual historical risk.

value.rationale: The primary September 2026 research paper explicitly asks whether the three Green representative languages are context-sensitive. This theorem resolves the upper-bound question simultaneously and much more strongly in deterministic logspace. In rank at least two the same paper proves neither language nor complement is context-free, so the upper bound locates genuinely non-context-free languages in a very low complexity class. The parity-of-edge-traversals mechanism provides a reusable method for tree-metric Green invariants. No claim is made about indexedness, optimal lower bounds, or arbitrary generating sets.
